turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
I didn't come to be thanked. Answer my question, Hale: who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
Can you read me your notes word for word?

I'll read you the dates: "Essay due Thursday, October 29. Zero entered Tuesday, November 3. Meeting today, Tuesday, November 10, 4:15." The rest of the page is my position, and you'll have that in writing. Now answer me, Hale: who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
Not those notes. Your instructions. What were you told to do in this meeting?

I'm not sure what you mean, Hale, and I have a client call in twenty-five minutes. What I came with is my son, and a zero he found out about on his phone. Who decided on it, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
What do you plan to say if I bring up your daughter?
You'll have my position in writing, Hale. If you want to find out what I'd say about my daughter, bring her up and see how it goes. Who decided on the zero?
